review.summary: This patch does three things at once and ships debug scratch to the tree. The JSON-schema flattening logic has been substantially rewritten to fix a real metadata-tracking bug, but the fix carries unprincipled cleanups: `JSON.stringify` equality checks inside the inner loop of schema finalization, a `play.ts` that imports from a relative source path and is clearly local debug, and a behavior change (overrideCount 6 -> 12) that is hand-waved by adjusting a test expectation instead of explained. The fileProcessor change is a nice piece of taste — shared props hoisted, anyOf reduced to only what differs — and would have been a clean standalone patch. Split this into three patches: (1) the parent-tracking fix in `to-json-schema.ts` + `schemas.ts` with the new test, (2) the fileProcessor refactor, (3) drop `play.ts` entirely or keep it out of the diff.

issues.description: play.ts committed as debug scratch with relative source import
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from `./packages/zod/src/index.js` instead of `zod/v4`, and the body is interactive console.log debugging of the bug under repair. This is the author's working scratchpad, not a patch. It should not be in the diff at all. Refuse the patch on this alone in any maintained tree; revert play.ts to its prior shape or drop it from the PR.

issues.description: One patch doing three unrelated things
issues.detail: This is THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one. (1) parent metadata tracking in to-json-schema.ts plus the wrapper-id test, (2) the fileProcessor hoist-shared-props refactor and its snapshot update, (3) the mini/schemas.ts parent:true enablement. They have independent justifications, independent risk, and independent bisect value. Split them. The fileProcessor change in particular has nothing to do with parent tracking and should land or be reverted on its own merit.

issues.description: Test expectation flipped from 6 to 12 with no explanation
issues.detail: `expect(overrideCount).toBe(6)` becomes `toBe(12)` with no comment in the test and no mention in the commit message. The test is literally titled 'override: do not run on references' — doubling the override count is exactly the failure mode that test was written to catch. The removal of the `if (!seen.isParent)` guard around `ctx.override` in finalize is the cause: overrides now run on parent schemas too. Either this is a regression and the test was right, or it's intended and the title is now a lie. Pick one and write the commit message.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used for property-equality inside finalize loop
issues.detail: Two new code paths use `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])` to decide whether to delete a property. This is slow, allocates per comparison, is order-sensitive on objects, and silently returns equal for things containing functions, undefined, or NaN. In a hot finalization loop over every seen schema this is the wrong tool. Use a structural-equal helper, or — better — track *which* keys came from inheritance vs were authored on the child so you don't have to guess. The whole `_cached` shadow-copy dance suggests the data model is missing a 'where did this property come from' field.

issues.description: BAD-TASTE: two near-identical de-dup loops with copy-pasted continue guards
issues.detail: The block at ~418 (de-dup against refSeen.def) and the block at ~444 (de-dup against parentSeen.def) are the same loop written twice, including the same `if (key === "$ref" || key === "allOf") continue;` skip and the same JSON.stringify equality. This is the textbook special-case-instead-of-generalizing smell. Extract one helper `removeInheritedKeys(target, source)` and call it twice; or, again, fix the underlying model so you don't need either copy. As written, the next maintainer has to keep these two blocks in sync forever.

issues.description: isParentRef logic deletes keys it didn't add
issues.detail: After `Object.assign(schema, refSchema); Object.assign(schema, _cached);` the new `isParentRef` branch walks every key on schema and deletes anything not in `_cached`. `_cached` is a snapshot of `seen.def ?? seen.schema` from before the merge — so any property the child had implicitly (added by an earlier processor pass before flattenRef ran) gets stripped. The 'child is a refinement so it inherits nothing' assumption is doing a lot of work here and is not documented in the code or commit message. At minimum write down the invariant; ideally don't reconstruct intent by set-difference.

issues.description: process() reorders parent handling without explaining the consequence
issues.detail: Previously, when a parent existed, the child's own processor was skipped — parent ran instead and child inherited via ref. Now child's processor always runs, then parent is processed and stored separately. That's a real semantics change: any processor that previously was bypassed for child schemas now executes. The fileProcessor diff in the same PR is probably one consequence; there may be others not covered by tests. The commit message says 'Improve metadata tracking' — that hides a behavior change that touches every wrapper schema.

issues.description: GOOD-TASTE: fileProcessor refactor eliminates a real duplication
issues.detail: The fileProcessor change pulls shared keys (contentEncoding, format, minLength, maxLength, type) up to the root and reduces each anyOf branch to just `{ contentMediaType: m }`. This is the linked-list-without-the-special-case version of the previous code. Land this as its own patch with a one-line message and it's an obvious accept.

issues.description: Commented-out `// { parent: true }` removed in mini without a note
issues.detail: The mini ZodMiniType change just uncomments the previously dead `{ parent: true }` argument. That's fine, but the original comment was presumably there for a reason — probably 'this broke something, revisit'. The commit message should say what changed that makes it safe now (presumably the new parent-tracking path), so the next person who wants to comment it out again knows the history.

issues.description: Seen.ref type widened from `| undefined | null` to `| null`
issues.detail: The type annotation for `ref` dropped `undefined`. Code in flattenRef still distinguishes 'ref === null' (sentinel for processed) from falsy-ref (no ref ever set). If `undefined` was previously a legal value somewhere this is a silent semantics narrowing. Confirm no caller reads `seen.ref` as undefined; otherwise document that null is now the only sentinel.
